learningObjective: Reason about how torch.compile handles in-place mutation of an object captured from the enclosing Python scope (a non-input tensor).

canonicalClaims.claim: TorchDynamo treats mutation of a captured (non-input) tensor as an external side effect: it either lifts the referenced tensor into the compiled region's inputs (with a runtime write-back at the boundary) or graph-breaks around the mutation, depending on what can be safely traced.
conditions: The referenced tensor is reachable through Python semantics that Dynamo can inspect.
nonImplications: Does not imply every capture-mutation compiles cleanly; complex control flow can graph-break.
Does not imply the mutation is free; boundary write-backs add cost.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Boundary write-backs or graph breaks impose real overhead.

misconceptions.claim: Any tensor not in the argument list cannot be mutated inside a compiled region.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Captured tensors can be handled via lifting; not universally forbidden.

misconceptions.claim: TorchDynamo rewrites the outer Python list on return via a dedicated hook.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The mechanism is write-back to the identified tensor object, not list-level rewriting.

implementationFacts: Lifted tensors show as extra inputs to the compiled region
Runtime wrapper writes back mutated tensors after the compiled call
Graph breaks may appear if the captured object cannot be safely lifted
performanceScenarios: Excessive capture-mutation across tight loops can cause repeated write-backs; refactoring to explicit inputs is a common tuning step.
